scope: Research candidates and issues; not runtime rulings or publication approval.

topics.title: Where do fencers restart?
topics.finding: Restart position depends on a scored touch, period start, ground held, contact or passing; correct fencing distance can affect a rear-line result.
facts: Was one foot already behind the rear line?
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Touch before Fence or after Halt
topics.finding: A new action cannot start after Halt; a movement already begun can remain valid subject to the specific stopping rule.
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Touch as time expires
topics.finding: Expiration of time is a distinct stop: linked clock preserves already registered touches; an unlinked timekeeper stop does not allow a launched hit to continue.
facts: Was the clock connected to the apparatus?
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Close distance and blades that cannot be used
topics.finding: Close quarters is permitted while weapons can be wielded correctly; corps à corps and inability to analyze the phrase cause a stop.
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Contact to avoid a hit versus ordinary contact
topics.finding: Intentional corps à corps to avoid a hit, jostling and brutal contact have different disciplinary consequences from ordinary contact.
facts: Was avoidance, jostling or violence established?
topics.publication_limit: Share reviewed consequences with the penalty guide; do not infer intent from the search phrase.

topics.title: Passed opponent and turning hit
topics.finding: Passing and passed fencers have different immediate-hit rights; complete passing triggers Halt, and sabre separately prohibits forward crossing.
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Ducked or touched the strip with a hand or knee
topics.finding: Ducking and target displacement are allowed; a touch during or after a fall is a separate annulment rule.
facts: Was it a duck or a fall?
Was the touch during/after the fall?
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Turned the back on the opponent
topics.finding: Turning the back is forbidden, but an immediate turning hit by the fencer who was passed has an explicit passing exception.
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Non-weapon hand, arm or electrical equipment
topics.finding: Using the free arm offensively/defensively and taking hold of electrical equipment are separately described offenses; cancellation accompanies them.
facts: Was target covered or equipment held?
topics.publication_limit: Penalty guide already covers much of this; link shared information rather than creating conflicting copies.

topics.title: One foot off the side
topics.finding: A completely off-side foot triggers Halt; an action begun before Halt can retain validity when only one foot is off.
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Both feet off the side
topics.finding: Both feet off annuls subsequent actions subject to the simple/immediate opponent-hit exception; épée and convention weapons differ.
facts: Was the opponent still on with at least one foot?
Was the response simple and immediate?
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Side exit near the rear line
topics.finding: The required retreat and attack-start position can place both feet beyond the rear line; accidental exits have an exception.
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Crossed the rear line
topics.finding: A touch is awarded against a competitor when both feet cross the rear limit completely.
facts: Which is the rear limit rather than end of conductive runoff?
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Left the side to avoid a hit
topics.finding: Avoiding a hit by leaving the side carries a separate first-group penalty and annulment; not every side exit establishes avoidance.
facts: Was avoidance established by the referee?
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Forced or accidental boundary exit
topics.finding: An involuntary accidental exit such as jostling incurs no boundary penalty; the contact itself may involve a different offense.
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Pool score, tied time and deciding hit
topics.finding: Normal pool bouts end at five or the time limit; tied time has a drawn-priority extra minute. Épée doubles at 4–4 and in the extra minute do not count.
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: DE score and tie at regulation time
topics.finding: Standard DE bouts use 15 touches or nine effective minutes, with a tied extra minute; domestic age formats must be checked separately.
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Double at the winning score
topics.finding: Pool 4–4 and DE tied final-score situations need their explicit end-of-bout rules, not a universal both-lights-each-scores summary.
topics.publication_limit: Include 10-touch/youth variants only after format-specific source confirmation; do not infer every adapted score rule by analogy.

topics.title: Épée doubles in the extra minute
topics.finding: USA notes specify no points for doubles in the deciding extra minute, with fencers retaining position.
facts: Is this the deciding extra minute?
Was there a double or a single valid touch?
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Team relay target, time and carryover
topics.finding: Relays have cumulative targets and time limits; an unachieved target carries the actual score into the next relay.
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Relay-ending hit and additional penalty hit
topics.finding: The rulebook allows a relay score beyond its usual five-touch increment when a valid last hit and an additional penalty hit occur together.
facts: Was a valid relay-ending hit registered?
Was an additional penalty awarded at the same time?
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Wrong relay order or substitution
topics.finding: Wrong bout order can annul touches scored since the change; replacement rules and announcements also matter.
topics.publication_limit: International and domestic team formats differ; use current domestic event format before applying o.99 wholesale.

topics.title: Veteran and youth format exceptions
topics.finding: Veteran 10-touch/two-period formats and domestic youth formats alter the target and sabre break point.
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Clock failed or remaining time questioned
topics.finding: Effective time, asking for remaining time and a referee estimate after clock/timekeeper failure are separately covered.
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Injury, cramp and withdrawal
topics.finding: Medical interruption and withdrawal require the applicable medical procedure; they are not automatic replay/score correction rights.
topics.publication_limit: Keep score consequences separate from medical advice; handbook withdrawal classification is its own topic.

topics.title: Lamp registration versus legal validity
topics.finding: Apparatus establishes registration; specific rules can annul registered touches. An unregistered normal hit cannot simply be awarded.
facts: Any applicable exception or penalty touch?
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Touched floor or another object
topics.finding: Touches on objects other than the opponent/equipment are disregarded; intentional false registration is separately penalized.
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Épée floor hit and grounded-strip testing
topics.finding: Observed location and demonstrated ground-circuit failure are distinct evidence. A successful later test does not establish where the original point landed.
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Which touch can equipment tests cancel?
topics.finding: Only the last registered touch, with the disadvantaged-fencer and timing requirements, is considered; no blanket replay of earlier touches.
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Preserve equipment and test immediately
topics.finding: Tests are immediate, referee-supervised and performed without unauthorized changes. A demonstrated fault need not recur every time; impossible tests have a separate rule.
facts: Why could tests not be performed?
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Blade broke during the touch
topics.finding: A broken blade of the fencer hit triggers the specified annulment unless the break clearly occurred after registration.
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Touch during or after a fall
topics.finding: Touches made during/after a fall are annulled; ducking with knee/hand contact and intentional falling to avoid a touch are distinct.
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Dropped weapon before Halt
topics.finding: Intentional dropping during the action has a second-group sanction; an opponent hit may remain valid if the action began before Halt.
facts: When was the opponent action started?
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Épée body, clothing and equipment target
topics.finding: Épée uses the point and whole-body/clothing/equipment target, with guard/ground apparatus and validity exceptions.
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Registered valid double versus invalid/doubtful double
topics.finding: Ordinary doubles score both; valid/invalid and established/doubtful doubles have distinct t.94.5 treatment.
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Guard hit caused a light
topics.finding: A guard/strip registration fault differs from oxidation, adhesive, paint or loose-tip exceptions that cannot justify annulment.
facts: Tip could be tightened/unscrewed by hand?
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Proper touch failed to register
topics.finding: Non-registration can justify annulment when tests and exceptions allow; it never creates a missing normal point.
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Light from a beat or equipment movement
topics.finding: Fortuitous registration unrelated to a proper touch is an equipment-failure scenario requiring controlled tests.
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: First light disappeared after second hit
topics.finding: A subsequent opponent touch suppressing the first fencer’s registered touch has an explicit failure clause.
facts: Was one registered touch annulled by the subsequent one?
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Unplugged connection and retaining device
topics.finding: Body-cord disconnection at hand/back has an exception tied to the back retaining device; connecting-cable faults and later reel tear-out are distinct.
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Épée point tore the conductive strip
topics.finding: A strip tear caused by a floor hit with simultaneous opponent registration has its own annulment clause.
facts: Did the point tear the strip?
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Foil target and white light
topics.finding: Foil point touches count on specified target including a bib portion; ordinary off-target stops the phrase without scoring.
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Covered or substituted foil target
topics.finding: Target covering/substitution has penalty and possible scoring exceptions beyond ordinary off-target rules.
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Foil false colored light or missing registration
topics.finding: Foil has its own failure list and priority-related exclusions. A permanent off-target or on-target-as-off-target condition does not automatically annul a priority hit.
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Attack, preparation, riposte and fencing time
topics.finding: Priority explanations need the action glossary; fencing time is an action concept, not the electrical lockout interval.
facts: What action did the referee identify?
topics.publication_limit: Written definitions are source-backed; modern borderline action classification needs current referee interpretation rather than a mechanical rule engine.

topics.title: Foil simple, compound and advance attacks
topics.finding: Arm extension, threat, feints and preparation distinctions are in the written attack conventions.
topics.publication_limit: Do not turn written text into an automatic ruling on a contested video; obtain current official interpretation for borderline preparation.

topics.title: Point in line and failed blade search
topics.finding: Preexisting point-in-line and failure to deflect/find the blade can change priority under weapon-specific conventions.
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Beat on weak versus strong blade
topics.finding: Beat location matters: foible and forte are treated differently in the weapon-specific priority rules.
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Immediate riposte and delayed renewal
topics.finding: A parry creates a riposte opportunity; immediacy, pauses and renewal of attack affect the relevant conventions.
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Stop hit during compound attack
topics.finding: A stop hit in time against a compound attack has an interval-of-fencing-time condition, unlike a stop hit into a simple attack.
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Simultaneous attacks versus faulty double
topics.finding: Foil/sabre distinguish simultaneous conception/execution from a faulty double action; lights alone do not distinguish them.
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Sabre target and ordinary off-target
topics.finding: Sabre permits cutting/thrusting to its defined target; ordinary non-valid target does not register or stop the phrase.
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Guard scoring and follow-through mask contact
topics.finding: Official domestic guidance distinguishes incidental follow-through mask contact, scoring with the guard, and a forceful/deliberate blow.
topics.publication_limit: Use the detailed February 2025 referee FAQ; it explicitly limits this interpretation to domestic sabre and does not license applying it to épée/foil.

topics.title: Sabre through-blade hit and whip-over
topics.finding: Written validity and apparatus suppression of whip-over are distinct; apparatus design does not itself decide priority.
topics.publication_limit: Read Appendix B C together with t.96.4; do not infer registration solely from a spectator’s view.

topics.title: Sabre equipment fault and insulation exception
topics.finding: Sabre has its own tests; nonconforming guard/handle/pommel insulation can prevent annulment even if a weapon hit registers.
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Sabre attack, forward crossing and priority
topics.finding: Sabre attack timing/threat, blade actions, immediate riposte and forbidden forward crossing form distinct questions.
topics.publication_limit: The official source library does not provide a complete current visual priority curriculum; detailed borderline classification remains a referee-review gap.

topics.title: Passed equipment check versus a fault during fencing
topics.finding: Initial checks and later failures/nonconformity are separate; passing inspection does not prove later equipment correctness.
topics.publication_limit: t.72 and t.20 updates are already audited; reuse docs/RULE-UPDATES-2026-10.md. USA clothing exceptions require domestic notes.

topics.title: Foil/épée tip weight, travel and body-cord tests
topics.finding: Tip force/travel, body cord, conductive target and sabre insulation specifications help explain tests, not retroactively prove an unseen touch.
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Conductive strip, runoff and guard grounding
topics.finding: Conductive runoff is not automatically legal fencing area. Circuit grounding and strip boundaries answer different questions.
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Electrical lockout and contact sensitivity
topics.finding: Appendix B gives different apparatus timing/sensitivity for each weapon, including an épée double-timing tolerance band.
facts: Apparatus registered one or two lights?
topics.publication_limit: Use the Appendix B entries in the source inventory; never equate an electrical timing band with foil/sabre fencing-time priority.

topics.title: Conductive bib used in épée
topics.finding: The handbook specifically prohibits foil/sabre conductive-bib masks in épée because they can ground the opponent tip.
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Point without a physical registered hit
topics.finding: Rear-line and penalty touches can change the score without an ordinary hit; penalty histories and annulment are separate.
topics.publication_limit: Reuse the established penalty data and current passivity update rather than duplicate progression logic in scoring.

topics.title: Non-combativity changes score and ends a bout
topics.finding: Completed October 2026 research already supplies current passivity guidance and exceptions; November text is historical here.
topics.publication_limit: Do not re-research. Reference docs/RULE-UPDATES-2026-10.md and db rule_updates; suppress historical progression as current.

topics.title: Final salute and reopening a completed bout
topics.finding: The rules distinguish a final scored touch from formal completion; t.37.3 prevents restarting a finished bout/relay even for a formal mistake.
facts: Has the bout/relay finished under t.122?
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Rule-application protest versus point of fact
topics.finding: Fact disagreement, rule application and other administrative protest are distinct; newer domestic operations text needs reconciliation with t.174.
facts: What accepted fact and definite rule?
topics.publication_limit: Current app’s universal Head Referee wording is incomplete in light of the 2026–27 Operations Manual p.15. Resolve and revise before treating the procedure as comprehensive.

topics.title: Official video request, allocation and finality
topics.finding: Official video is a separate procedure: requester, allocations, retained successful challenges and final reviewed decision are specified. Domestic availability is not the FIE mandatory-event schedule.
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Wrong recorded score or disputed scoresheet
topics.finding: Domestic handbook and Operations Manual describe scoresheet review, presence/agreement, documentation and deadlines separately from touch-call review.
facts: Transcription error or disputed bout score?
topics.publication_limit: Use handbook pp.82–83 and Operations Manual p.18; personal video/photo evidence is not accepted as score documentation in the handbook procedure.

topics.title: Victories, indicator and touches scored
topics.finding: Pool rankings order victories/bouts, touch differential and touches scored, with draw rules for absolute ties. Domestic format controls promotion.
topics.publication_limit: Confirm the complete clauses, current domestic applicability and wording before publishing.

topics.title: Withdrawal/exclusion effects on pool results
topics.finding: Withdrawal, ordinary exclusion and passivity loss cannot be conflated; domestic handbook classification rules need their own scope.
topics.publication_limit: Handbook distinctions and current passivity rules must be read together; do not apply a historical generic black-card paragraph to P-black.
